# Audio and speech understanding

<!-- Generated by scripts/catalog.py from data/models.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

[← Model index](../README.md#models)

**Reviewed as of 2026-09-12 · 44 entries.**

Speech/audio-conditioned language models that produce text. Speech prompts, audio reasoning and voice-chat input do not by themselves imply speech output.

**Modalities:** T = text, I = image, V = video, A = general audio, S = speech, M = music, X = other structured modalities. A is a broad label, not a guarantee of every audio task. See the [methodology](../docs/methodology.md) for interaction labels, variant scope and inclusion rules.

Dates below refer to the linked paper or announcement, **not necessarily a weights/API release**. An em dash means no date was established from the reviewed source.

## Model notes

<a id="audio-flamingo"></a>

### Audio Flamingo

Focuses on sound understanding, in-context examples and textual dialogue.

<a id="audio-flamingo-2"></a>

### Audio Flamingo 2

Non-speech sound/music understanding and long-audio reasoning.

<a id="audio-flamingo-next"></a>

### Audio Flamingo Next

General audio understanding and temporally grounded reasoning.

**Listed variants:** AF-Next.

<a id="audio-cogito"></a>

### Audio-Cogito

A reasoning-trained audio-language model.

<a id="audio-deepthinker"></a>

### Audio-DeepThinker

Trains reasoning chains to remain grounded in acoustic evidence.

<a id="audio-reasoner"></a>

### Audio-Reasoner

Learns explicit reasoning from audio-question-answer data.

<a id="audiochatllama"></a>

### AudioChatLlama

Uses spoken prompts for instruction-following and language tasks.

<a id="blsp"></a>

### BLSP

Aligns speech-conditioned and text-conditioned language behavior.

<a id="blsp-emo"></a>

### BLSP-Emo

Preserves speech emotion in the language model's responses.

<a id="desta"></a>

### DeSTA

Preserves nonlexical speech information through descriptive supervision.

<a id="desta2"></a>

### DeSTA2

Speech instruction-following without dedicated speech instruction-tuning data.

<a id="desta2-5-audio"></a>

### DeSTA2.5-Audio

General audio model intended to preserve the text backbone's language abilities.

<a id="diffa"></a>

### DIFFA

Speech-conditioned text generation with a diffusion LM.

<a id="diffa-2"></a>

### DIFFA-2

Extends DIFFA to broader audio understanding and practical decoding.

<a id="duplexmamba"></a>

### DuplexMamba

Simultaneously processes speech and generates text; a deployed spoken interface needs a speech-output component.

<a id="gama"></a>

### GAMA

Reasoning over non-speech sounds and nonverbal audio.

<a id="llark"></a>

### LLark

Music description, understanding and reasoning.

<a id="llasm"></a>

### LLaSM

Accepts spoken instructions; speech generation is not implied by its name.

<a id="ltu"></a>

### LTU

Open-ended sound understanding beyond fixed classification labels.

<a id="ltu-as"></a>

### LTU-AS

Joint speech content, paralinguistic and non-speech audio understanding.

<a id="mellow"></a>

### Mellow

Small model trained for audio-grounded reasoning.

<a id="meralion-audiollm"></a>

### MERaLiON-AudioLLM

Singapore-focused multilingual and paralinguistic speech understanding.

<a id="midashenglm"></a>

### MiDashengLM

Uses general audio captions to align speech, sounds and music with text.

<a id="moss-audio"></a>

### MOSS-Audio

Timestamped audio understanding and text generation.

<a id="mu-llama"></a>

### MU-LLaMA

Music question answering and captioning; separate from MuMu-LLaMA.

<a id="music-flamingo"></a>

### Music Flamingo

Analyzes music and songs; does not serve as a music generator here.

<a id="musilingo"></a>

### MusiLingo

Music captioning and textual responses to music questions.

<a id="omni-r1-audio-reasoning"></a>

### Omni-R1 (audio reasoning)

Rouditchenko et al.; distinct from the two-system Omni-R1 and R1-Omni.

<a id="osum"></a>

### OSUM

Speech recognition, emotion, speaking style and other speech-understanding tasks.

<a id="pengi"></a>

### Pengi

Casts audio tasks as free-form text generation.

<a id="qwen-audio"></a>

### Qwen-Audio

General audio input with textual answers.

**Listed variants:** Base; Chat.

<a id="qwen2-audio"></a>

### Qwen2-Audio

Voice-chat mode accepts speech but generates text, not audio.

**Listed variants:** Base; Instruct.

<a id="salm"></a>

### SALM

Speech recognition and translation with in-context examples.

<a id="salmonn"></a>

### SALMONN

General hearing model for speech, sounds and music.

**Listed variants:** 7B; 13B.

<a id="salmonn-2"></a>

### SALMONN-2

Uses general-purpose self-supervised representations for hearing tasks; separate from video-SALMONN 2.

**Listed variants:** 8B.

<a id="slm-google"></a>

### SLM (Google)

The named model from 'Bridge the thin gap'; SLM is also a generic abbreviation elsewhere.

<a id="soundwave"></a>

### Soundwave

Reduces the representation and sequence-length gap between speech and text.

<a id="speechverse"></a>

### SpeechVerse

Multi-task audio-language instruction-following and generalization.

<a id="step-audio-r1"></a>

### Step-Audio-R1

Audio reasoning release; consult later R1 variants for spoken interaction support.

<a id="step-audio-r1-5"></a>

### Step-Audio-R1.5

The report improves reasoning and alignment for open-ended audio tasks; no speech output is asserted.

**Listed variants:** R1.5.

<a id="textpro-slm"></a>

### TextPro-SLM

Preserves both recognized words and prosodic embeddings for language reasoning.

<a id="ultravox"></a>

### Ultravox

Model emits text; a deployed voice agent adds a separate speech synthesizer.

**Listed variants:** Release family; model cards identify checkpoints.

<a id="voxtral"></a>

### Voxtral

Audio chat and spoken-content understanding; separate from Voxtral transcription-only releases.

**Listed variants:** Mini; Small.

<a id="wavllm"></a>

### WavLLM

Combines linguistic and speaker-related speech features.
